title: GA4 alternatives for GDPR
description: A shortlist of Google Analytics 4 alternatives when EU privacy, consent banners, or data residency are the reason you are switching.

sections.title: Why teams look past GA4
sections.content:
GA4 is free and deep, and it is tied to Google's advertising stack. Teams leave when they want fewer consent prompts, data stored outside Google, or a dashboard someone will actually open.

This page is a shortlist, not legal advice. Confirm the setup with counsel for your visitors and your contracts.

sections.title: Four alternatives that cover most switches
sections.content:
**Plausible** and **Fathom** — hosted, cookieless web analytics for blogs and marketing sites. Start here if you need pages, referrers, and a few goals. Compare them in [Plausible vs Fathom](/compare/plausible-vs-fathom/).

**Umami** — open-source web analytics you can self-host. A fit when you want a simple dashboard and you are willing to run it. See [Google Analytics vs Umami](/compare/google-analytics-vs-umami/).

**Matomo** — the closest GA-like suite, as Matomo Cloud or On-Premise. Choose it when ecommerce, custom dimensions, or data on your own servers matter. See [Google Analytics vs Matomo](/compare/google-analytics-vs-matomo/) and [Matomo vs Plausible](/compare/matomo-vs-plausible/).

sections.title: How to pick in one sitting
sections.content:
1. If you still need Google Ads attribution, keep GA4 for ads and add a privacy-first tool for the public site — or accept the consent work and stay on GA4.
2. If the site is content or marketing only, pick Plausible or Fathom and estimate cost in the [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/).
3. If the data must live on your servers, shortlist Umami or Matomo On-Premise.
4. Read the matching comparison before you migrate. The verdicts and pricing context stay on those pages.

sections.title: What you give up
sections.content:
Lightweight alternatives do not include BigQuery export, Google Ads native attribution, or GA4's exploration depth. Matomo gets closer on reporting and still will not be a Google Ads product.

Script weight is a separate decision. Our recorded numbers, including Umami, are in the [script performance matrix](/learn/analytics-script-performance/). Matomo is not in that matrix until we record it.
